problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 20 public infrastructure projects to maximize the total projected benefit to the community. The profile for each project is as follows:
* Project A: projected benefit is 0.032, community disruption is 0.191, allocation bounds [0.067, 0.526]
* Project B: projected benefit is 0.196, community disruption is 0.127, allocation bounds [0.047, 0.531]
* Project C: projected benefit is 0.076, community disruption is 0.084, allocation bounds [0.017, 0.585]
* Project D: projected benefit is 0.054, community disruption is 0.167, allocation bounds [0.078, 0.487]
* Project E: projected benefit is 0.145, community disruption is 0.201, allocation bounds [0.099, 0.613]
* Project F: projected benefit is 0.117, community disruption is 0.032, allocation bounds [0.009, 0.618]
* Project G: projected benefit is 0.080, community disruption is 0.054, allocation bounds [0.080, 0.830]
* Project H: projected benefit is 0.031, community disruption is 0.222, allocation bounds [0.015, 0.805]
* Project I: projected benefit is 0.104, community disruption is 0.091, allocation bounds [0.016, 0.873]
* Project J: projected benefit is 0.048, community disruption is 0.086, allocation bounds [0.087, 0.867]
* Project K: projected benefit is 0.083, community disruption is 0.040, allocation bounds [0.032, 0.800]
* Project L: projected benefit is 0.121, community disruption is 0.241, allocation bounds [0.090, 0.727]
* Project M: projected benefit is 0.061, community disruption is 0.180, allocation bounds [0.005, 0.804]
* Project N: projected benefit is 0.133, community disruption is 0.232, allocation bounds [0.051, 0.636]
* Project O: projected benefit is 0.187, community disruption is 0.106, allocation bounds [0.044, 0.594]
* Project P: projected benefit is 0.069, community disruption is 0.234, allocation bounds [0.066, 0.773]
* Project Q: projected benefit is 0.168, community disruption is 0.182, allocation bounds [0.033, 0.711]
* Project R: projected benefit is 0.176, community disruption is 0.090, allocation bounds [0.050, 0.635]
* Project S: projected benefit is 0.125, community disruption is 0.244, allocation bounds [0.012, 0.561]
* Project T: projected benefit is 0.075, community disruption is 0.263, allocation bounds [0.056, 0.509]
Each project must receive a fraction of the total budget that lies within its specified minimum and maximum allocation bounds, and the sum of all budget fractions must equal one. To ensure timely completion, the planner requires that the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by the subset Q = {T}, collectively receive at least 0.057 of the total budget. Furthermore, the overall community disruption index for the portfolio must not exceed 0.213, and the total projected benefit must be no less than 0.085. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total projected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
